name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Pulse Carbine PC-6 'Heartbeat'
description: A compact electromagnetic pulse weapon that fires focused EMP bursts capable of disabling unshielded electronics within a targeted cone. The PC-6 generates a shaped electromagnetic wavefront through a series of rapidly discharged capacitor banks, creating a pulse that induces catastrophic current surges in electronic circuits. Against cyberware, the effect ranges from temporary shutdown to permanent damage depending on the target's shielding grade. Arcturus designed it for anti-drone and counter-electronics operations, but its effectiveness against augmented personnel has made it a weapon of terror in aug-heavy communities.
specifications: pulse type: Shaped electromagnetic wavefront effective range: 5-25 meters cone capacitor recharge: 6 seconds between pulses pulses per charge: 8 weight: 3.2 kg electronics kill radius: Unshielded systems within 15m cone cyberware effect: Temporary shutdown (shielded) to permanent damage (unshielded)
story_hooks: An underground movement is using stolen PC-6 units to disable surveillance networks in liberated neighborhoods — but the pulses are also frying residents' medical cyberware.
Someone has modified a PC-6 to emit a specific frequency that only affects Axiom-manufactured neural interfaces — this is targeted corporate warfare.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist angular carbine with a distinctly asymmetrical profile. The weapon tapers from a bulbous, heat-sink-laden receiver to a narrow emission barrel. Its silhouette evokes something between a medical imaging device and a military targeting system—clinical and predatory.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 68 cm. Barrel section: 22 cm. Width across capacitor housing: 11 cm. Height with sight rail: 14 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Noticeably front-heavy despite moderate total weight—the capacitor banks and emission matrix pull toward the barrel. Feels dense, purposeful, slightly unbalanced for prolonged one-handed operation.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum chassis with integrated copper capacitor housings. Carbon-reinforced polymer foregrip and stock. Heat-dissipation fins are brushed steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal aluminum with oxidized copper accents around the capacitor vents. Fingerprint-resistant coating shows micro-scratches from field use. Heat fins have a distinctive burnt-orange patina from electromagnetic stress discharge.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with oxidized copper highlights. Accents of deep orange around active cooling zones. Black polymer furniture.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with subtle diamond-knurl texturing for wet/augmented-hand purchase. Cool to the touch due to active heat dissipation into the stock.
distinctive_features: Pronounced copper cooling fins wrapping the capacitor banks—visually dominant
Narrow emission aperture with electromagnetic dampening grilles forming a subtle honeycomb pattern
Three stacked LED indicator strips (charge status) along the left receiver—amber, blue, red
Exposed capacitor cycling relay visible through translucent side panel—pulsing indicator of charge state
Electromagnetic resonance dampers: small metal rings spaced along the barrel
Iron Point Ammunition stamp: raised serif lettering on the magazine well
Arcturus Defense Solutions corporate logo: a stylized compass rose etched into the receiver
Faint scorch marks around ventilation ports from decades of pulse discharge
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Iron Point Ammunition nameplate stamped in serif font on the magazine well area. Arcturus Defense Solutions compass-rose logo etched below the charging handle. Serial number embossed on the rear of the aluminum chassis in small numerals. Safety warnings in standardized military iconography molded into the polymer furniture.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually encountered in mid-to-heavy field condition—cosmetic aluminum scoring from gear contact, oxidized copper with visible discharge burn patterns, and evidence of regular capacitor stress. Functional firearms are meticulously maintained internally but show exterior weathering consistent with restricted military/security deployment.
